title: Region strobe: intermittent region loss + fair-share load-shedding exercise
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Run a targeted chaos experiment that 'strobes' a region (rapid intermittent network/availability toggles) while simultaneously inducing GPU-pool resource pressure and dependency blackholes. The goal is to validate: 1) graceful multi-region failover during rapid reconfiguration, 2) tenant fair-share shedding behavior under oscillating capacity, and 3) correct circuit-breaker and fallback routing behavior without violating critical SLOs. This ticket covers design, safety gates, automated orchestration, monitoring, and a post-run analysis writeup.
hypothesis: If the control plane and serving runtime handle frequent partial region flaps and transient GPU exhaustion while running the fair-share shedding policy, then: failover will keep >99.5% of production-critical reads within p99 latency budget, tenant-level fairness will prevent starvation of small-tenancy workloads, and circuit breakers will prevent dependency cascades. If not, we will observe unfair error amplification, unbounded retry storms, or SLA violations concentrated on low-priority tenants.
success_criteria: Global availability > 99.9% for control-plane heartbeats during the run window
Production-critical model endpoints: p99 latency degradation <= 2x baseline during worst oscillation
Tenant-level error amplification detection: no tenant experiences >5x baseline error rate for more than 10 minutes
Fair-share verification: at least 90% of shed decisions match the configured policy across 1,000 synthetic tenants
Circuit-breakers trigger and open within configured thresholds and recover without manual intervention
test_plan: 1) Prep: create sandbox tenant slice with 1,000 synthetic tenants and baseline load profiles; wire in traffic shaping and sampling. 2) Safety window reservation and Canary: run a short smoke strobe (30s toggles for 5 minutes) against non-prod region pair (us-west-2 <-> us-east-1). 3) GPU pressure: inject a memory-leak helper into a subset of GPU nodes to simulate progressive pool exhaustion and forced OOM throttles. 4) Dependency blackholes: introduce two types - an immediate 503 storm for upstream feature-store and a hanging TCP proxy for auth service to simulate timeouts. 5) Strobe sequence: perform 12 cycles of intermittent region isolation (30s isolated / 90s recovered) while GPU pressure ramps. 6) Observability: collect traces, rate-limited logs, per-tenant shed decisions, and runtime metrics. 7) Recovery: at end of sequences, run controlled ramp to steady-state and validate automatic healing. 8) Post-run: gather artifacts and draft findings and remediation list.
safety_controls: Run during pre-approved maintenance window; page duty lead before start
Automated kill-switch in control plane to stop chaos if global error rate > 2% for 5 minutes
Limit blast radius to tagged sandbox project IDs and a single region pair
Rate limit injected faults and cap GPU-leak nodes to <= 15% of pool
Manual permission gating: only two engineers (assignee + safety buddy) can start the run
Dry-run smoke tests required and sign-off from Product on customer-impact tolerance
